text:
The overhaul was supposed to tighten things up. John Chayka took over as general manager in May, Craig Berube was replaced by Jim Hiller, Gavin McKenna arrived first overall and Sergei Bobrovsky signed. Twenty-one games in, the Maple Leafs are 8-11-2, winless in five (0-5-0, all at home) and outscored 22-9 in that run. The chances say the slide is real: Toronto has had 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) in those five games and 46% all season.

Bobrovsky has not been the fix, with an .857 save percentage and 4.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, all losses. The Leafs have even scored about six and a half more goals than their chances predicted. Our numbers give them a 5% chance at the playoffs.

The noise around the stars is loud. A headline had captain Auston Matthews calling out teammates after the Devils loss, William Nylander is fielding trade talk while insisting, in TSN's words, "It's not that slumpy," and McKenna's growing pains have drawn scrutiny of the coaching staff. Injuries to Kirill Marchenko, Max Domi and others haven't helped.

The one line working is Jack Roslovic, Matthews and Easton Cowan, 9-2 in goals together. Roslovic (14 points in 10 games, 7.9 expected) is riding a heater. The top pair of Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh has been underwater, with 43% of the expected goals.
headline: A homestand from hell for the new-look Leafs
